chunks: 3415 - Al-Washsha' narrated from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"And Dāwūd and Sulaymān, when they judged concerning the field."

He عليه السلام said: "The judgment of Dāwūd عليه السلام was the ownership of the sheep, and what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made Sulaymān عليه السلام understand was that he judged for the owner of the field by granting him the milk and wool for that entire year."

key_terms.الصُّوفِ: the wool as part of the benefit awarded
key_terms.الْحَرْثِ: the cultivated field or crop that was damaged
key_terms.بِاللَّبَنِ: by granting the milk as compensation
key_terms.رِقَابَ الْغَنَمِ: the sheep themselves as property ownership
key_terms.فَهَّمَ: made to understand with divinely granted insight
key_terms.يَحْكُمَانِ: they were judging in a legal dispute

ai.seo_question: How did Sulaymān عليه السلام interpret the case of the sheep and the field differently from Dāwūd عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic account of the judgment of Dāwūd and Sulaymān عليهما السلام regarding a damaged field. It clarifies that Dāwūd عليه السلام judged by awarding the sheep themselves, while Sulaymān عليه السلام was given understanding by Allah to award the field's owner the sheep's milk and wool for one year. The report highlights divinely guided judicial discernment in resolving property damage.
